brief: How to raise your first round — 6 lessons from a 2nd-time founder.

slots.headline: How to Raise Your First Round: 6 Lessons From a Second-Time Founder
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Build Relationships Early
slots.body: Investors bet on lines, not dots. Start building trust six months before you need the check, and warm intros will convert faster than cold emails.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Story Beats Data
slots.body: Your deck is not a spreadsheet. Craft a compelling narrative around the problem, your insight, and the future you are uniquely positioned to build.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Pick the Right Partner
slots.body: Chasing the highest valuation can backfire. Optimize for aligned incentives and an investor who will actually pick up the phone when things break.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Prep Your Diligence Room
slots.body: Due diligence delays kill momentum. Have a clean data room ready before the first meeting so you can capitalize on investor excitement immediately.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Speed Creates FOMO
slots.body: A slow round signals weakness. Run a tight fundraising process with a clear timeline to force decisions and create competitive urgency.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.title: Cash in the Bank
slots.body: Term sheets are just paper. The round is not done until money hits the bank, so keep backup options alive until the wire clears.
slots.author: STUDIO N

slots.headline: Ready to Close Your Round?
slots.body: Download the full fundraising checklist and avoid the mistakes that slow first-time founders down.
slots.author: STUDIO N
